armorSets.name: Guardsman's Armour
armorSets.purpose: the standard armour choice for poleaxe users, being the heavy armour set that is built out of the Rare Armour Schematic (wiki). Amya's OP field: "Best Armour before Epic schem: Guardsman."

armorSets.name: Flameshackle
armorSets.purpose: on poleaxe pushback and the old billhook work with flameshackle armor and block break anything you touch with those abilities. - house playbook

armorSets.name: Fearless Paladin Armour
armorSets.purpose: provides CC immunity during your ultimate, adds +10% HP, boosts Weapon Dance damage reduction by 75% of the base value ("so its 75% of 25% (not +75% flat)").

spells.fillerNotes: 4th slot is flexible: The Old Billhook is popular for its knockdown on a low cooldown. Bec de Corbin is good AoE, strong vs units. Grim Harvest removes control effects and damages block heavily, but has slow attack speed and poor AoE. Halberdier's Thrust is unpopular due to its poor AoE and lack of control effects (wiki). Glass Cannon build swaps in Halberdier's Thrust (vs heroes) or Bec de Corbin (vs units).

builds.name: Tanky + Full Unit CC
builds.summary: Focuses on crowd control, locking down enemy heroes and units for extended periods. Key skills: Push Back, Weapon Dance, The Old Billhook, plus the Lochaber Strike ultimate. "will help you win a lot of units trade"
builds.altSkill: Rough Justice can replace Lochaber Strike as the ultimate for lone dangerous heroes - it inflicts Winded, which can't be blocked, and grants a burst of mobility the class otherwise lacks; little use in other situations though (wiki).

builds.name: Full Damage
builds.summary: Emphasizes maximizing damage at the cost of defense. Uses Push Back, The Old Billhook, and either Halberdier's Thrust (vs heroes) or Bec de Corbin (vs units).
builds.forWhom: Amya's own label for this build: "troll."
builds.altSkill: Ultimate: Lochaber Strike recommended for burst, though both ultimates are viable depending on the situation.

matchups.why: wiki: many weapon classes have a great advantage against nodachi in duels - Chain Dart & Scimitar, Dual Blades, Poleaxe, and Pike all named.

wiki (Musket page): Musket users cannot deal large amounts of damage or control effects against units consistently compared to other melee classes such as the nodachi and the poleaxe - Poleaxe is one of the stronger anti-unit melee classes.

Amya's DB guide: "In the current meta, where Poleaxe, Nodachi, and Shortsword are dominant, having your cleanse is non-negotiable" - Poleaxe named among the CCi-Divers classes that punish a no-cleanse DB build.
wiki: heavy armoured, low-mobility classes like Maul and Poleaxe are at a disadvantage dueling Musket users - unless Rough Justice is active (its burst of mobility offsets the gap).

wiki: Lochaber Strike's control effects land across multiple hits, so some weapon classes can escape the skill or stun you out of it, particularly before the final hit which has a longer delay than the others.

Amya's Stalwarts guide: CCi (Stand Fast) is their reset button vs a "polearm" ulting them - resets both their block bar and any CC on them. "Polearm" is ambiguous house shorthand, read here as Poleaxe per the alias sweep but not confirmed as this class specifically.

matchups.vs: A tank Poleaxe anchoring a Longsword
matchups.why: PA is one of the house's named tank anchors a Longsword player pairs with to absorb/pull focus. - house playbook
jc008titanSQ: play alongside your zealots/paladins in sieges and block break every stalwart with Push Back + The Old Billhook - helped turn 70 unit kills into 200 in a single fight. - house playbook

matchups.vs: Damage-dealing units the hero enables while controlling the fight
matchups.why: No explicit "which units does a Poleaxe player bring in their own warband" list was found anywhere in this sweep. [GAP: Poleaxe's own-warband unit pairings - vets/house question]

techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - For braced units like Forte, Halberds, Phalanx - niche: enemy hero outnumbered, unaware or afk.

techniques.name: Shift-auto-attack stagger chain
techniques.rhythm: Amya: for classes without cleanse (or cleanse on cooldown) - Rotate one shift-auto-attack between each CC application to keep the chain going; exact rotation depends on your spell set. Amya's own example, verbatim: "dismount - shift aa - push back - shift aa - billhook - shift aa - blabla or w/e."

techniques.name: Old Billhook roll-cancel
steps: roll immediately after the hit connects
follow up with another skill or a sprinting attack
techniques.rhythm: wiki: animations are slow, so animation-canceling matters more than ever for Poleaxe - a poleaxe user can use The Old Billhook and then cancel the animation directly after dealing damage by rolling, allowing the user to follow up immediately with another skill or a sprinting attack (wiki, verbatim).

techniques.name: Lochaber Strike camera-steering
steps: steer with the camera, not the character
catch enemies coming from different directions
techniques.rhythm: lets you redirect the hit toward enemies approaching from other angles - A poleaxe user can change the direction of Lochaber Strike simply by moving the camera (wiki, verbatim).

gameplay.text: Poleaxe users can easily and effectively stun units in a large AoE and also duel well against most other hero weapon classes, but have low mobility and slow attack animations.

the poleaxe is considered to be one of the strongest weapon classes due to its very high capability to deal out control effects and the ability to equip heavy armour while still boasting respectable damage.

sources.source: Amya's CB Library Discord, #Heroes-Forum, thread "Poleaxe Guide"

patchNote: Amya OP posted 08/10/2024, last edited 26/03/2026 - about three months before the 25/06/2026 Chaos patch. Single OP post, no thread replies, so no post-patch update exists in this source.
roleLabel: The poleaxe is a two-handed polearm focused around dealing large amounts of control effects against both units and heroes.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight:

bullets.text: Poleaxe is one of the two named tank anchor classes a Longsword player pairs with to absorb and pull focus.
Weapon Dance and Lochaber Strike are great skills to stop charging cavalry and disrupt units in general.

if you have the resources, give it a try in sieges. Play alongside your zealots/paladins and see how much more you can do, even supporting other people does a LOT - helped 70 unit kills to 200 in a single fight, just by being there and block breaking every stal.
"When I play cannons I swap to poleaxe on supply" - a habit of switching into Poleaxe specifically to hold/defend a supply point while operating artillery.
instantly removes you from CC while stunning enemies hit - a crucial survival and disruption tool.

Poleaxe's entire kit of CC skills --except pin--, per BirdOfQin's active-blocking rundown. "Pin" isn't a canonical ability name - the wiki confirms Rough Justice's first hit "cannot be blocked," the one CC effect that gets through.
once you've used Push Back, Weapon Dance, etc., you have a window where you're weaker. If all your CC abilities are on cooldown, a crafty enemy can exploit that moment.
Keep your ultimate to CC non-CCi units, or CCi units during their down time.

statSpreads.spread: Full Armor/HP attribute points; wiki: put character skill points into Toughness to further boost defenses.
Full STR attribute points; wiki: putting points into Strength to further boost damage is "another viable option."
